A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FENCE study and contain readable text, equations, six figures, eight tables, and Appendices A–C. No material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original evaluator and generator experiments in Sections 3–4, including benchmark results, ablations, manual data-quality evaluation, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–4, analyses in Figures 4–6, and appendix case studies.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.2 retain the same critique and document augmentation, evaluator objective, response revision procedure, and SFT/DPO training. The added inference description does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: The training datasets in Table 5 and evaluations on LLM-AggreFact, FActScore, and TruthfulQA are unchanged. The new RAG discussion introduces no evaluated dataset or scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 3, and 4 retain the same comparators, including SFT, Self-Eval-SKT, EVER-Pref, and FactTune-FS. Section 4.1 newly explains excluded alternatives without adding or removing evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Previously stated splits, metrics, model configurations, and evaluation procedures are retained, including FActScore's 400/100 training/test prompts and TruthfulQA's 703 test examples. New prompt and decoding descriptions disclose settings without revising an earlier specification.

E4.justification: The augmentation and training-recipe ablations, manual accuracy checks, popularity/topic breakdowns, revision-iteration and top-k analyses, and Appendix C case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are retained. For example, FENCE's average BAcc remains 74.7 in Table 1, and Llama3 E/R + Coarse retains 65.41% on FActScore and 67.14% on TruthfulQA in Table 3. Figures 4–6 and appendix examples are unchanged.

T1.justification: The evaluator mappings, label definitions, training objectives in Equations 1–2, and preference-pair calculation are unchanged. Mathematical display spacing changes, but no definition, assumption, derivation, or proof is revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same evaluator and generator-training contributions and performance claims. The added comparison rationale does not redefine the core contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 adds a rationale for excluding RAG based on inference-time knowledge access and differing objectives, expands the latency-based rationale for excluding inference-time methods, and asserts potential compatibility with them. Existing result interpretations and Section 7 limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies the biography prompt, 'tell me a bio of <entity>', and standard random decoding at inference. These are limited documentation additions; appendix implementation details and training/test split access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds Lewis et al. (2020) on retrieval-augmented generation and explicit positioning against RAG and inference-time approaches in Section 4.1. Li et al. (2024c) and Chuang et al. (2024) were already cited; Section 5 is unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 adds two explanatory paragraphs to Section 4.1 and a new Section 8 Acknowledgement. The remaining narrative, existing section order, and appendix prose are retained.

P2.justification: Spacing and vertical placement around figures and equations change, with subsequent column and page reflow. The same figures and tables retain their graphics, captions, and structures; appendix pages render identically.

improvement.justification: V3 modestly improves transparency by explaining comparator exclusions and documenting the biography prompt and inference decoding in Section 4.1. The scientific evidence and appendices are unchanged. The added latency and compatibility arguments receive no new empirical validation, so the improvement is limited to clearer scope and documentation.
